title: Maple Town mysteries for grade three

storyNoDigits: The mayor keeps the town records in a safe.
The lock shows a picture of blocks: big blocks, long blocks, and small blocks.
storyDigits: The mayor keeps the town records in a safe.
The lock wants hundreds, tens, and ones blocks.

storyNoDigits: Two friends share one fare on the streetcar.
One friend already holds part of the fare in tickets.
storyDigits: Two friends share one fare on the streetcar.
One friend already holds some of the tickets.

storyNoDigits: The suspect left a trail across the muddy yard.
Footprints sit in neat rows. Count the rows to find the hiding spot.
storyDigits: The suspect left a trail across the muddy yard.
The footprints form an array of equal rows.

storyNoDigits: The bake sale needs a fair pie.
Six friends share one pie. Every part must be the same size, so every friend gets a fair share.
storyDigits: The bake sale needs a fair pie.
Cut the pie into equal parts. Fractions are equal shares of a whole.

storyNoDigits: The culprit leaves a trail of pinecone piles.
Each pile grows by the same rule. Say the rule, then find the next pile.
storyDigits: The culprit leaves a trail of pinecone piles.
Each pile grows by the same rule. Predict the next pile.

storyNoDigits: The diner needs the right jug of juice for the recipe.
Count the cupfuls the recipe asks for.
storyDigits: The diner needs the right jug of juice for the recipe.
The recipe pours a set number of cupfuls.

storyNoDigits: The trophy was taken in a folding crate.
A flat net was left behind. Match it to the crate.
storyDigits: The trophy was taken in a folding crate.
A flat net was left behind. Count its faces to find the crate.

storyNoDigits: The fair booth hides a spinner with coloured slices.
Some colours cover more of the dial. Those land more often.
storyDigits: The fair booth hides a spinner with coloured slices.
Bigger slices are more likely. Smaller slices are less likely.

storyNoDigits: Detectives pay a small fee at the snack stand.
The fee is shown in the coin picture. Pay the same amount.
storyDigits: Detectives pay a small fee at the snack stand.
The fee is shown in coins. Pay the same amount with your own coins.

storyNoDigits: The librarian stacks returns on a rolling ladder.
Build the stacks that match the ladder picture.
storyDigits: The librarian stacks returns on a rolling ladder.
Build the stacks: hundreds, tens, and ones blocks.

storyNoDigits: Vehicles line up for the maple bay ferry.
The queue sits in neat rows. Count the rows to board.
storyDigits: Vehicles line up for the maple bay ferry.
The queue forms equal rows. Count the rows.

storyNoDigits: The busker played fiddle outside the bakery.
The tip is shown in the coin picture. Pay the same amount.
storyDigits: The busker played fiddle outside the bakery.
The tip is shown in coins. Pay the same amount.

storyNoDigits: Two keepers counted the boats in the harbour.
Both keepers counted at the same hour.
storyDigits: Two keepers counted the boats in the harbour.
Whose count was bigger?

storyNoDigits: The ferry logs every rider aboard.
Two logs were found from the same sailing.
storyDigits: The ferry logs every rider aboard.
Which log counts more riders?

storyNoDigits: The parade route passes the boundary gate.
One marshal counted before the gate and one after.
storyDigits: The parade route passes the boundary gate.
Which count is bigger?

storyNoDigits: The bridge crew has one pallet of bricks and then another arrives.
storyDigits: The bridge crew has one pallet of bricks and then another arrives.
Build the sum of the two pallets.

storyNoDigits: The cider press filled one barrel in the morning and another by noon.
Ten small blocks make one long block, and ten long blocks make one big block.
storyDigits: The cider press filled one barrel in the morning and another by noon.
Build the sum. Remember to regroup.

storyNoDigits: The harbour held a full count of crates this morning.
Some crates shipped out on the noon boat.
Ten small blocks make one long block, and ten long blocks make one big block.
storyDigits: The harbour held a full count of crates this morning.
Some crates shipped out on the noon boat.
Build the difference. Remember to regroup.

storyNoDigits: The print shop stacked papers for the whole route.
The route used up some of the stacks.
Ten small blocks make one long block, and ten long blocks make one big block.
storyDigits: The print shop stacked papers for the whole route.
The route used up part of the stacks.
Build the difference. Remember to regroup across the zero.

storyNoDigits: The chowder house fills its big kettle for the ferry day.
Count the cupfuls the recipe asks for.
storyDigits: The chowder house fills its big kettle for the ferry day.
The recipe pours a set number of cupfuls.

storyNoDigits: Two tally boards hang at the general store.
Both boards counted the same day.
storyDigits: Two tally boards hang at the general store.
Which board counts more?

storyNoDigits: The rink keeps a record board for the longest skate.
Two seasons are written side by side.
storyDigits: The rink keeps a record board for the longest skate.
Which board holds the bigger record?

storyNoDigits: The rain gauge filled past one mark in the spring and past another by the fall.
Ten long blocks make one big block, so regroup as you build.
storyDigits: The rain gauge read one amount in the spring and more in the fall.
Build the year total.

storyNoDigits: The skate shed started with a full wall of rentals.
The thaw sent most of them home, so regroup twice to build what is left.
storyDigits: The ice rink held a full count of skate rentals.
Half the rentals went home. Build what is left.

storyNoDigits: The post office sorted one sack in the morning and another after lunch.
The morning sack was nearly full, so the piles join across a new big block.
storyDigits: The post office sorted one sack in the morning and another after lunch.
Build the day total.
